bounded-context.name: Catalog
bounded-context.purpose: The browse-and-discover surface of the store. Owns product vocabulary, variant structure, and the SKU value type that every other context uses to refer to "the thing being sold."

term.name: `Product`
term.definition: A thing the store sells, abstracted from its purchasable variants. "iPhone 17 Pro" is a Product; "iPhone 17 Pro / 256GB / Titanium" is a . Customers browse Products; they buy Variants.
term.identity-rule: Stable by `productId` (UUID, issued on creation). A Product survives renames, description rewrites, and variant churn.

term.name: `ProductVariant`
term.definition: A specific purchasable form of a Product — a (size, colour, configuration) tuple resolved to one SKU and one price. Stock, shipping weight, and tax classification live on the Variant, not the Product.
term.identity-rule: Stable by `(productId, variantId)`. A Variant's SKU may change across business reorganizations; the variantId never does.

term.name: `SKU`
term.definition: A short opaque string identifying a Variant for fulfillment purposes. Used by every downstream context (Orders, Inventory, Shipping) as the cross-context handle for "the thing being sold." Distinct from 's identity: a Variant *has* a SKU, but a Variant might exist briefly with no SKU assigned (during onboarding).
term.equality: By string value. Uppercase ASCII; hyphens allowed; max 32 chars.

term.name: `categorizeProduct`
term.definition: Assigns a Product to a taxonomy node (electronics/phones, apparel/shoes/running, …) based on its attributes and the active taxonomy version. The taxonomy is part of the Catalog model; external taxonomies (Google Shopping Categories, FB Catalog Feed) are mapped at the integration boundary, not here.
term.returns: A taxonomy-node fqid plus a confidence score in [0, 1]. Confidence below 0.6 routes to manual review.

term.name: `ProductListed`
term.definition: Emitted when a Product transitions from `draft` to `published` and becomes visible on the storefront. The event is the public signal for downstreams to start indexing, pricing, and stock-checking.
term.emitted-when: `Product.status` transitions `draft → published`, and at least one with a non-null exists.
term.payload: `{ productId, defaultVariantId, listedAt }`. The full Product snapshot is fetched via the open-host-service seam below; the event carries pointers, not state.

term.name: Published state
term.definition: The conceptual condition under which a Product appears in the storefront browse surface and a Variant becomes purchasable. Not a single enum field — depends on Product.status, Variant.sku presence, and the active taxonomy. Modeled as a concept rather than a value because the calculation isn't a single function.

term.name: `Bundle`
term.definition: Historical: a fixed pre-priced group of Variants sold as one SKU (e.g. "starter kit"). Replaced in 2025 by promotion-based bundling managed in the (unmodeled) Promotions context. The slug is retained because legacy events and historical orders still reference it.

invariant.name: SKU is unique across the catalog
invariant.statement: No two s share a . The uniqueness constraint is enforced at write time, not after.
invariant.rationale: Duplicate SKUs break every downstream — Inventory can't tell which stock pool to deduct from; Orders can't decide which Variant a LineItem refers to. Catching duplicates at write time is much cheaper than reconciling after.

seam.name: Catalog ↔ Downstreams
seam.description: Catalog exposes a stable read-only API: list products, fetch by productId, fetch by SKU. Orders, Inventory, Shipping all consume this API without negotiating with Catalog's team. New downstreams can be added without changing Catalog.
seam.rationale: Catalog's data shape changes slowly relative to the rate at which downstreams want to read it. Publishing a public read surface and requiring downstreams to conform decouples the release cadence and keeps Catalog from carrying knowledge of every consumer.

boundary-rule.rule: No downstream context writes to Catalog data. Orders cannot retroactively rename a Product; Inventory cannot mark a Variant unavailable in the Catalog model.
boundary-rule.rationale: Letting downstreams mutate Catalog would push consumer-specific concerns into the public model and silently break other consumers. Stock state belongs in ; sale availability belongs in Orders' projection of Catalog — neither belongs in Catalog itself.

module.name: Product tree
module.description: The Product → Variant → SKU chain. Read together when reasoning about how the store represents "what's for sale." Other atoms (categorize, listings) attach to this chain but aren't part of its core shape.
module.rationale: Beginners coming to the codebase often miss that SKU is a value type, not an entity — the module groups them visibly so the identity/value distinction shows up at the cluster level.
